## 2. What to build

**§12 Channels: lifecycle and who may do what** (prototype frames 3, 4, 7)
- **Announcement channels:** only managers post, replies included; members react or use **"Reply privately"**, which opens a direct message to the author with the post quoted (CH50). A post pings every member once, even on Mentions and replies; only Nothing silences it.
- **Private channels:** invisible to anyone not in them; managers (and admins) add people (CH58); someone who leaves can't rejoin unless added. **Removal** writes a quiet line in the person's Catch up ("Sofia removed you from Launch"), no ping; the channel leaves their sidebar (CH61).
- **Delete** moves a channel to Recently deleted for 30 days (managers and admins; General can't be deleted); Restore brings it back; the purge is final. **Archive** makes it read only, labelled, still searchable; its Catch up items clear.

**§15 Settings, and where each thing lives**
- **Settings → Members → Roles:** the chat switches of PERM-7 plus "Add custom emoji"; "Start calls" hidden until Meet ships.

**§12 table rows**
| Action | Admin | Manager | Author | Member | Viewer | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| React | ✓ | ✓ | — | ✓ | ✓ | CH60 |
| Archive, unarchive | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — | §12 |
| Delete, restore a channel | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — | CH62 |
| Make private | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — | CH59 |
| Announcement switch | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — | CH23a |
| Add people to a private channel | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — | CH58 |
| Remove people | ✓ | ✓ | — | leave only | leave only | CH61 |
| Add, remove managers | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — | §6 #11 |

**Edge cases this block handles** (§Edge cases)
- A viewer → reads, reacts, receives direct messages, can't post or start one; the composer shows a line, not a box; Catch up's `R` opens nothing to type into.
- A member posts in an announcement channel → refused with "Only managers post here · Reply privately"; a manager's post pings everyone once.
- A public channel made private → non-members lose it (their Catch up items for it close); keys lose it unless "Include private channels I'm in" and the creator is a member; it never goes back to public.
- Someone is removed from a private channel → a quiet Catch up line; the channel leaves their sidebar; they can't rejoin unless added; the channel's messages stop arriving in their store within one access check.
- A channel is deleted → Recently deleted for 30 days (managers and admins see it; Restore brings everything back); the purge is final; General refuses.
- The last manager leaves → the channel passes to the workspace owner if they can read it, else its earliest remaining member; a manager can't un-manage themselves while last.

## 3. Acceptance criteria

**AC10 — Channels and permissions**
- **AC10.1** §12's table holds row by row (the SQL tests run as owner, admin, manager, member, viewer, outsider and a key)
- **AC10.4** announcement channels post only for managers, flip later, Reply privately
- **AC10.5** delete to Recently deleted for 30 days with Restore; archive stays searchable
- **AC10.6** removal writes the quiet line and the channel leaves the sidebar
- **AC10.7** the last manager rule
- **AC10.9** viewers react and receive, never post.

**AC5 — A PM's week**
- **AC5.5** an announcement channel pings everyone once and offers "Reply privately"

**AC6 — An agency's week (internal chat)**
- **AC6.2** a private channel is invisible to non-members and its managers add people
- **AC6.3** a public channel becomes private once, never back

**AC1 — Trust pass (v1's fourteen trust bugs, REPLAN §1.3 B)**
- **AC1.12** managers can be added, the announcement switch flips later, "Manage any channel" is read, "Start calls" is hidden

**Tests that prove them** (file · name · AC · plain English)

- `supabase/tests/chat_lifecycle.test.sql` · "private, delete, archive, removal" · proves AC10.4–10.6, AC6.2, AC6.3 · Public → private once; delete to Recently deleted with Restore and a purge after 30 days; General refuses; archive is read only and searchable; removal writes the quiet line.
- `supabase/tests/chat_announce.test.sql` · "announcement channels" · proves AC5.5, AC10.4, AC1.8 · Members' posts are refused; a manager's post reaches every member once even on Mentions and replies; the switch flips later; Reply privately opens a direct message with the post as a card.

## 4. Decisions that bind it

`share_op_announce` is live (v1's switch; the privacy migration `20261014090000`, on the build branch) and `chat_op_set_announcement` replaces it; CV-23 drops it. Full permissions table with op names: round-3 §2.4; #13: ops read `chat_channel_managers` and "Manage any channel", not admin alone.

- **New ops** (round-3 §2.3, #13, #25; activity rows `chat.manager_add`/`_remove`, `announcement`, `channel_private`, `channel_delete`/`_restore`, `channel_archive`, #15): `chat_op_set_manager(channel, user, on)` (the person must be in the channel; **the last manager can't be removed**), `chat_op_set_announcement(channel, on)` (channels only, never DMs), `chat_op_make_private(channel)` (public → private, one way, keeps current members; those who read it without joining lose it and their Catch up items for it close, `done_how = 'closed'`), `chat_op_delete_channel(channel)` (stamps `deleted_at/by`; General refuses; DMs use leave; **touches every member's membership row** so it reaches them live), `chat_op_restore_channel`, read `chat_recently_deleted(ws)` (managers and admins), daily job `chat-purge-deleted` (hard delete after 30 days; messages, Catch up items and links cascade; files go with AT-1's trash clock; the registry row becomes a tombstone). Archive (CV-2b's op) now also closes the channel's open Catch up items and keeps its linked item's line marked archived.
- **Removal and adding:** removal (CV-2b stamps `left_at`/`removed_by`) writes a quiet `removed` Catch up line, "Sofia removed you from Launch", no ping; adding writes `added`, "Mike added you to Launch"; the channel leaves the removed person's sidebar; a private channel can't be rejoined unless added.
- **Announcement channels** (§12; CH23a, CH50): members can't post, replies included; a manager's post pings every member once (the `announcement` fan-out, CV-5) and only Nothing silences it. **Reply privately** = `chat_op_open_dm` with the post's author, then a send carrying the post as `moduo://chat_message/<id>` (a card: CV-10's reference; before CV-10 lands it draws as a plain link).
- **Make private confirm** (one ask, #33): "Make Founders private? It can't go back to public. 4 people stay in it."
- **Viewers** react (`chat_op_react` lets readers, CH60) and receive direct messages but never post or start one.
- **Role editor** (§15, #13): the chat switches live once, in `src/features/settings/access/role-editor.tsx` / `permission-matrix.tsx` (read `chat_caps_get`/`chat_caps_set`; defaults in `src/features/sharing/rules.ts` `CHAT_CAP_DEFAULTS`); "Start calls" stays a column and is hidden; **`add_emoji`** (`workspace_chat_caps`, `CHAT_CAPABILITIES`; on for admins and members, off for viewers): CV-20 adds it (it is built first after the line, CH16b); CV-15 only shows it and adds nothing to the migration for it. If the catalog lacks the column when you start, hand back "blocked on CV-20".

## 7. Watch out

- Run every op as owner, admin, manager, member, viewer, outsider and a key.
- **Tier 2** (migrations, RLS, contracts, moduo-mcp, src/lib/runtime*): one `/code-review high` and one security scan of the diff at the end; scan findings go only into the hand-back.
- **Migration:** stamp provisional (re-cut on apply day, chat's order kept); redefine from live bodies (`pg_get_functiondef`); re-state grants by name (`DROP` + `CREATE` resets them); re-assert the Realtime publication if you publish a table; apply only on your migration turn, then `bun run db:test chat`; never `local:reset` or `migration up` (runbook, `docs/gotchas/supabase.md`).
- **Hot files:** `src/features/chat/store/*`, `src/lib/runtime.chat.web.ts` and `src/features/settings/access/*`. Keep edits there small; another builder may change them too.
- **Public repo:** describe no security weakness in any file; tell the orchestrator in the hand-back.
